audit_findings.title: The 0% convertible creates an uncharged cash claim while its proceeds are added as equity cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.25 billion principal and 4.762 million initially underlying shares; a mechanical principal deduction with removal of those shares reduces bear/base/bull value per share from $37.41/$42.73/$48.98 to approximately $25.88/$31.48/$38.05
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge retains cash but does not deduct the mandatory principal cash claim, while OE bears no regular interest charge and the share denominator treats the entire conversion amount as equity dilution.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon conversion, the Company will settle conversions by paying cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the 2030 Notes to be converted and paying or delivering, as the case may be, cash, shares of common stock or a combination of cash and shares of common stock, at its election, in respect of the remainder, if any, of its conversion obligation in excess of the aggregate principal amount of the 2030 Notes being converted, based on the applicable conversion rate(s).
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated internal inconsistency. The omitted principal equals 29.9% of base equity value. Existing full-share dilution partly offsets the overstatement but is inconsistent with cash settlement of principal and does not cure it.
audit_findings.action: Rerun all scenarios by retaining bridge-date cash, recognizing the $1.25 billion principal cash claim, and calculating only excess-value dilution after applying the conversion terms and capped calls.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method stakes appear to be counted both in owner earnings and in the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $74.911 million of 2025 equity-method income and $171.7 million added as stakes_net; the bridge addition alone equals $1.76 per diluted share and 4.1% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method income enters the OE numerator through reported net income, while the bridge separately adds the value of the corresponding investments.
audit_findings.evidence: A portion of this segment's operations is also conducted through joint ventures, which typically earn fees, and we account for them following the equity method of accounting.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting pathway for double counting is demonstrated, but the record does not identify every component of stakes_net. If the bridge amount represents the same operating investees, value is overstated; recurring equity-method income is also 31.0% of the $241.8 million OE anchor, making the treatment consequential.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $171.7 million stakes_net amount by investee against the $164.708 million bridge-date Investments in Unconsolidated Affiliates balance and the OE worksheet; then either remove corresponding earnings from OE and value the stakes separately or retain the earnings and remove their bridge value.

audit_findings.title: The forecast perimeter is inconsistent with the signed medical divestiture
audit_findings.magnitude: transaction value up to $800 million; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Closing would remove medical-business OE and reinvestment needs from the forecast while adding net proceeds and a retained minority interest to the bridge, subject to taxes, costs, transferred liabilities and stranded overhead.
audit_findings.evidence: This segment also manufactures and supplies products for diagnostic imaging and radiotherapeutic treatments and is a partner for contract development and manufacturing services for life science and pharmaceutical companies.
audit_findings.explanation: No completed disposal or discontinued-operations presentation exists at the bridge date, so AS_FILED is not a demonstrated historical error. The signed transaction is nevertheless a forward-looking perimeter change potentially large relative to the $4.177 billion base equity value; the opposing effects cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: At closing, rebuild OE for the retained perimeter and update the bridge for actual net proceeds, retained interest, taxes, transaction costs, transferred liabilities, debt repayment and stranded costs; invoke the too-hard review if those amounts cannot be isolated.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded retirement obligations are an additional claim on equity cash flows
audit_findings.magnitude: $152.0 million gross underfunding at June 30, 2026, equal to $1.55 per diluted share and 3.6% of base equity value; unrecoverable amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Required contributions consume equity cash without necessarily reducing future net income when previously accrued; alternatively, the unrecoverable funded-status deficit belongs in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had underfunded defined benefit pension and postretirement benefit plans with obligations totaling approximately $153.3 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The gross deficit is filed, but substantial postretirement costs may be recoverable under U.S. Government contracts and periodic benefit costs and contributions may already affect OE. The record therefore does not establish the net incremental claim or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile plan-by-plan funded status, expected contributions and Government recovery rights at June 30, 2026 to the OE calculation; deduct only the unrecoverable claim or explicitly model the associated net cash contributions.

audit_findings.title: Environmental and decommissioning accruals may produce cash outflows not captured by future OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $107.2 million total accrual at December 31, 2025 and $103.880 million noncurrent environmental liabilities at June 30, 2026; net unrecoverable amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Settlement of previously accrued environmental and asset-retirement liabilities can consume cash without a matching future earnings charge, requiring either an OE cash-flow adjustment or a net bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025 and 2024, we had total environmental accruals, including asset retirement obligations, of $107.2 million and $103.4 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: A filed liability exists, but substantially all decommissioning costs at two Government Operations facilities are contractually covered by the DOE, while other obligations may be indemnified or supported by restricted cash and financial assurance. The supplied record does not separate those recoveries from BWXT's net exposure or establish whether settlement cash is already captured in OE.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the bridge-date total accrual roll-forward and separate DOE-recoverable, indemnified and restricted-cash-supported amounts; reconcile expected settlement cash flows to OE and deduct or model only BWXT's net unrecoverable obligation.
